note: 35.0's corpus: invented items shaped like DCLab's memory (facts about people, the workspace and ten projects, know-how, episodes). No customer's data; the testers named are invented. One line each, at most 300 characters.

items.text: Answer the owner in simple everyday words, short sentences, one idea each, and give a real example for every hard idea.
The owner wants honest, critical answers: say what is wrong with a plan and show a better way instead of agreeing.
Persian text for the owner goes in an HTML page with the Vazirmatn font, right to left, 20 px, line height 2.1; English and code stay left to right.
The owner allows live model runs of at most half a euro each; every run prints its cap first and reports what it spent.
Only Claude models may be used; the OpenAI key stays in the file but its provider is blocked.
The owner likes long jobs to run in the background while work goes on, as long as they can be resumed.
Never stash or reset the owner's working folder: unfinished documents are kept there on purpose.
Mina, a tester, works in logistics and prefers results as a short table with the business cost next to each number.
Mina reads English well but asks questions in Persian; reply in English unless she writes a whole message in Persian.
Reza, a tester, is a data analyst who wants the code of every step so he can rerun it in his own notebook.
Reza dislikes long explanations of leakage; he asks for the check's result and the column it flagged, nothing more.
The owner's Mac has 8 GB of memory: keep heavy jobs one at a time and stop when free disk falls under 2 GB.
The owner plans to fine-tune a small open model later on a bigger Mac, so every agent step is kept whole as training data.
Sara, a tester from a bank, may not upload customer tables; she works only with synthetic data built from her description.
This workspace uses Anthropic Claude Sonnet as its model for every agent role.
Use for training is switched off in this workspace until the owner turns it on per project.
Model spend in this workspace is capped at 18 euros a month for the collector.
Raw uploads in this workspace are deleted after 30 days; cleaned tables and records are kept.
Projects in this workspace store their data in PostgreSQL, not in files.
The team in this workspace has three roles: owner, ML engineer and viewer; only ML engineers and the owner approve stages.
Notebook cells may be run by any signed-in member of this workspace for now.
Sign-in is required in this workspace; API tokens are given per person.
This workspace's reports are written in English with a Persian summary page.
Evaluations in this workspace always start with an empty memory.
Telco churn: the target is whether a customer cancels within the next 30 days after the snapshot date.
Telco churn: the prediction is made on the first day of each month, from data known by the end of the previous month.
Telco churn: the column total_charges is cumulative and includes the month being predicted, so it was dropped as a leak.
Telco churn: the business can call 200 customers a month, so the decision uses a capacity of 200 calls.
Telco churn: a saved customer is worth about 300 euros a year; a retention call costs 5 euros.
Telco churn: the owner chose recall at the call budget as the main measure, not accuracy.
HyperAck fares: final_customer_fare and final_biker_fare are known only after the trip ends, so they never enter the model.
HyperAck fares: duration is measured after the trip, so it is a leak; the estimated duration at booking may be used.
HyperAck fares: the target is the price offered at booking time, predicted in euros.
HyperAck: ride and rider identifiers are dropped; they let the model memorise riders instead of learning prices.
HyperAck: trips are split by time, the last four weeks held out, because prices drift with fuel costs.
HyperAck: the Rating column is given by the customer after the ride, so it cannot be used to predict the fare.
Delivery fraud: a fraud case is an order the courier marked delivered but the customer reported as never received.
Delivery fraud: reviewers can check 16 rides a day; the model ranks orders and the top 16 go to review.
Delivery fraud: the same courier appears in many orders, so folds are grouped by courier to avoid optimistic scores.
Delivery fraud: the refund_issued column is set after the complaint, so it leaks the label and was removed.
Delivery fraud: a missed fraud costs the order value; a wasted review costs about 4 euros of staff time.
Delivery fraud: fraud is about 2 in 100 orders, so precision at the review budget is reported, not accuracy.
Ticket routing: each support ticket must go to one of six teams; the target is the team that finally closed it.
Ticket routing: the first team assigned is known at prediction time; the team that closes the ticket is not.
Ticket routing: ticket text is in English and Persian, so the text features must handle both scripts.
Ticket routing: a ticket sent to the wrong team costs about one hour of handling.
Ticket routing: the resolution_notes field is written when the ticket closes and must not be used.
Delivery time: the target is minutes from order to door; the model predicts it when the order is placed.
Delivery time: order_value is the basket's worth in euros and is used to weigh late deliveries in the decision.
Delivery time: weather is joined from the hour of the order, never from the hour of delivery.
Delivery time: the error measure is the mean absolute error in minutes, with a 90 percent interval.
Delivery time: the courier's actual pickup time is known only later and was dropped.
Retail returns: the target is whether an item is returned within 30 days of delivery.
Retail returns: one customer can have many orders, so the split keeps each customer's orders on one side.
Retail returns: duplicated order lines were found; the duplicates were removed before splitting.
Retail returns: the size_exchanged flag is set during the return and was removed as a leak.
Retail returns: the shop wants to warn buyers of high-risk items before checkout.
Bank marketing: the call duration column is known only after the call, so it is excluded from the model.
Bank marketing: the target is whether the client subscribed to a term deposit.
Bank marketing: the bank calls the top fifth of clients by score each campaign.
Bank marketing: the model search took close to five minutes on the laptop; the default budget was kept.
Card fraud: frauds are about one in six hundred payments; a fold must hold at least one fraud, so the search was skipped.
Card fraud: the features are anonymous components, so the explanations name components, not business fields.
Card fraud: time is in seconds from the first payment; the last two days are the holdout.
Card fraud: average precision is the main measure because the positive class is very rare.
Pump maintenance: there are no failure labels, so anomalies are found without labels and reviewed by an engineer.
Pump maintenance: the engineer can inspect ten alerts a week; the review list has ten rows.
Pump maintenance: confirmed alerts become labels, turning the project into a rare-event problem later.
Pump maintenance: sensor readings arrive every minute and are averaged by hour before detection.
Subscription retention: two actions exist, a discount and a call; each customer gets at most one.
Subscription retention: discounts are limited to 100 a week and calls to 40 a day.
Subscription retention: uplift was estimated from last year's random campaign, not from churn scores.
Subscription retention: later customers leave more often, so the interval is read from the latest fold.
Subscription retention: the realised value fell above the interval's centre on most seeds; the cause is still open.
Write the prediction moment and the error costs before looking at any score.
Fit every cleaning, encoding and selection step inside the training folds only.
Read the holdout once, after every choice is made; a second look makes its number optimistic.
When one person, courier or customer appears many times, group the folds by that entity.
A column filled in after the outcome, such as a refund or a closing note, is a leak even if it looks harmless.
Identifiers make a model memorise rows; drop them unless the problem is about that entity's history.
With a rare positive class, report precision at the budget or average precision, never accuracy alone.
When the data drifts over time, split by time and keep the latest period as the holdout.
Remove duplicated rows before splitting, or the same row lands in training and test.
A cumulative total that includes the target period leaks the future; use the total up to the cutoff.
Join outside data, such as weather, by the time of the prediction, never by the time of the outcome.
When the review team has a fixed capacity, choose the operating point by expected value under that capacity.
Give every reported number its interval and the assumption behind it.
Never call a model ready for production from benchmark results alone.
If a search budget runs over on a busy machine, the last attempt finishes late; the budget stops new attempts only.
A model search that does not beat the default by more than its interval stays switched off.
Synthetic tables keep the traps of the real table but never copy a real row.
When labels are missing, start with anomaly detection and turn confirmed alerts into labels.
Ask the person for the business cost of each kind of mistake before choosing a threshold.
A text column written by staff after the event, like resolution notes, must be dropped.
Check the row count after every join; a join that multiplies rows usually hides a key problem.
Uplift needs a past random experiment; churn scores alone do not say who will respond to an offer.
With two actions and separate capacities, assign each row the action with the higher value until each capacity is used.
Learning curves on training folds tell whether more rows would help; never read the holdout for it.
When the gate of an experiment is fixed before the run, a failed result is reported as failed, not adjusted.
Ask one question at a time, the one that unblocks the most next steps.
A sealed evaluation set is read once; tuning on it turns it into a development set.
Average sensor data to the decision's time step before modelling, so noise does not dominate.
A target defined as the final state of a ticket hides a leak when earlier states are features.
Prefer a simpler model when two are tied within their intervals.
Run 12 on Telco churn failed at the cleaning stage because the date column had two formats.
The first HyperAck run scored too well; the review found final_customer_fare among the features.
fraud_decision_v2 failed on width: the review interval was about a quarter too narrow.
fraud_decision_v3 passed after the interval came from holdout-sized samples of one fold.
The intern stopped mid-run when the worker restarted during a code change; the worker now waits for running jobs.
Sign-in failed because no account existed yet; the owner created one with the accounts command.
search_v3 crashed on card fraud because a fold had no fraud; the search is now skipped with a reason.
search_v3 on bank marketing ran 4.81 minutes against a 4.5 minute budget on a busy machine.
time_decision_v2 passed for the share capacity after reading the interval from the latest fold.
A store run was paused because free disk fell below 2 GB while swap grew.
The first routing model used resolution_notes and reached 97 percent; after removing it, 71 percent.
A commit once took another session's staged files because the whole index was committed.
